title: Constant pullback unit on continuous maps
statement: Let $i:Y_0\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $M$ be an abelian group with the discrete topology. For $W\in Y_{\acute et}$ and $g\in\underline M_Y(W)$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], let $\lambda_Y(g):|W|\to M$ be the continuous-map representative of $g$, let $\eta(g)\in (i_*i^*\underline M_Y)(W)$ be the inverse-image adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and let $c:i^*\underline M_Y\cong\underline M_{Y_0}$ be the constant-sheaf comparison [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Then $\lambda_{Y_0}(c(\eta(g)))=\lambda_Y(g)\circ|\operatorname{pr}_1|$ as continuous maps $|W\times_Y Y_0|\to M$. There is no finiteness hypothesis on $M$.

proof.text: Use the already proved continuous-map model of the constant abelian sheaf in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.ConstantSheaf (constantSheafIsoContinuousMapSheaf and toSheafify_constantSheafToContinuousMapSheaf). Define κ on g by precomposing its continuous-map representative with pr1. It is additive by pointwise addition. Naturality follows from the base-change square, Hom.etale_map_left_comp_fst.

Compose the constant-sheaf adjunction on Y with i^* ⊣ i_* and the terminal-object comparison for pushforward. The constant-sheaf comparison is the uniqueness isomorphism between this adjunction and the constant-sheaf adjunction on Y₀. Mathlib Adjunction.homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app and homEquiv_naturality_right identify the adjunct of c followed by the continuous-map comparison with the adjunct of the continuous-map comparison on Y₀.

The adjunct of κ, followed by the terminal-object comparison, sends m to the constant function m, because toSheafify_constantSheafToContinuousMapSheaf sends the presheaf unit to the constant function. The same holds on Y₀, and restrictions preserve constant functions, including on empty objects. Equality follows by evaluation at m and at a point of the terminal scheme. Cancel the terminal comparison isomorphism and use injectivity of the constant-sheaf adjunction Hom equivalence to identify κ with the adjunct of c followed by the continuous-map comparison. Evaluate this identity at W and g and expand homEquiv_unit to obtain the formula.
